raw: CHAPTER XIX. An Opinion
en: [Chapter 19] An Opinion

raw: Worn out by anxious watching, Mr.
en: Exhausted by his anxious watch, Mr.
ko: 근심스러운 감시로 지친 로리

raw: Lorry fell asleep at his post.
en: Lorry fell asleep at his post.
ko: 씨는 자신의 자리에서 잠이 들었다.

raw: On the tenth morning of his suspense, he was startled by the shining of the sun into the room where a heavy slumber had overtaken him when it was dark night.
en: On the tenth morning of his suspense, he was startled by the sun shining into the room, where a heavy sleep had overtaken him when it was still dark.
ko: 조바심 속에 맞이한 열흘째 아침, 아직 어두울 때 덮쳐온 깊은 잠에 빠져 있던 그는 방 안으로 비쳐드는 햇살에 깜짝 놀랐다.

raw: He rubbed his eyes and roused himself; but he doubted, when he had done so, whether he was not still asleep.
en: He rubbed his eyes and woke up, but at first he doubted if he was actually awake.
ko: 그는 눈을 비비고 깨어났지만, 처음에는 자신이 정말로 깨어있는 것인지 의심했다.

raw: For, going to the door of the Doctor’s room and looking in, he perceived that the shoemaker’s bench and tools were put aside again, and that the Doctor himself sat reading at the window.
en: Looking into the Doctor’s room, he saw that the shoemaker’s bench and tools were put away, and the Doctor himself sat reading by the window.
ko: 박사의 방을 들여다보니, 구두 만드는 작업대와 도구들은 치워져 있었고 박사 자신은 창가에 앉아 책을 읽고 있었다.

raw: He was in his usual morning dress, and his face (which Mr. Lorry could distinctly see), though still very pale, was calmly studious and attentive.
en: He was dressed in his usual morning clothes, and his face, though still very pale, looked calm and focused.
ko: 그는 평소의 아침 옷차림을 하고 있었으며, 얼굴은 여전히 매우 창백했지만 차분하고 집중한 모습이었다.

raw: Even when he had satisfied himself that he was awake, Mr.
en: Even when he was sure he was awake, Mr.
ko: 자신이 깨어있다는 것을 확신했을 때조차, 로리

raw: Lorry felt giddily uncertain for some few moments whether the late shoemaking might not be a disturbed dream of his own; for, did not his eyes show him his friend before him in his accustomed clothing and aspect, and employed as usual; and was there any sign within their range, that the change of which he had so strong an impression had actually happened?
en: Lorry felt uncertain for a few moments whether the shoemaking had been a dream. His friend sat before him in his usual clothes and appearance, working as normal, with no sign that any change had occurred.
ko: 씨는 구두를 만들던 일이 꿈은 아니었을까 잠시 불확실하게 느꼈다. 그의 친구는 평소의 옷차림과 모습으로 그의 앞에 앉아 아무런 변화가 일어났던 흔적도 없이 평소처럼 일하고 있었다.

raw: It was but the inquiry of his first confusion and astonishment, the answer being obvious.
en: It was just the question born from his initial confusion and shock, since the answer was already obvious.
ko: 대답이 이미 명백했기 때문에, 그것은 단지 그의 초기 혼란과 충격에서 비롯된 의문일 뿐이었다.

raw: If the impression were not produced by a real corresponding and sufficient cause, how came he, Jarvis Lorry, there? How came he to have fallen asleep, in his clothes, on the sofa in Doctor Manette’s consulting-room, and to be debating these points outside the Doctor’s bedroom door in the early morning?
en: If he wasn't reacting to something that had actually happened, then how did he, Jarvis Lorry, end up there? How had he fallen asleep in his clothes on the sofa in Doctor Manette’s consulting room, and why was he debating these points outside the Doctor’s bedroom door early in the morning?
ko: 만약 그가 실제로 일어난 일에 반응하는 것이 아니었다면, 도대체 어떻게 그, 자비스 로리가 그곳에 있게 되었단 말인가? 어쩌다 그가 마네트 박사의 진찰실 소파에서 옷을 입은 채로 잠들었으며, 왜 이른 아침 박사의 침실 문 밖에서 이런 점들을 두고 고민하고 있단 말인가?

raw: Within a few minutes, Miss Pross stood whispering at his side.
en: Within a few minutes, Miss Pross stood whispering at his side.
ko: 몇 분 안에, 프로스 양이 그의 곁에 서서 속삭였다.

raw: If he had had any particle of doubt left, her talk would of necessity have resolved it; but he was by that time clear-headed, and had none.
en: If he had any bit of doubt left, her words would have cleared it up, but by that time he was thinking clearly and didn't have any.
ko: 그에게 일말의 의심이라도 남아있었다면 그녀의 말로 말끔히 풀렸겠지만, 그 무렵 그는 명확하게 생각하고 있었고 어떤 의심도 가지지 않았다.

raw: He advised that they should let the time go by until the regular breakfast-hour, and should then meet the Doctor as if nothing unusual had occurred.
en: Lorry advised that they should wait until the usual breakfast hour and meet the Doctor as if nothing had happened.
ko: 로리 씨는 평소의 아침 식사 시간까지 기다렸다가 마치 아무 일도 없었던 것처럼 박사를 만나야 한다고 조언했다.

raw: If he appeared to be in his customary state of mind, Mr.
en: If he seemed to be in his usual state of mind, Mr.
ko: 만약 그가 평소의 정신 상태인 것처럼 보인다면, 로리

raw: Lorry would then cautiously proceed to seek direction and guidance from the opinion he had been, in his anxiety, so anxious to obtain.
en: Lorry would then carefully ask the Doctor for his professional opinion on the case.
ko: 씨는 그 사건에 대한 박사의 전문적인 소견을 조심스럽게 물어볼 작정이었다.

raw: Miss Pross, submitting herself to his judgment, the scheme was worked out with care.
en: Miss Pross agreed, and they carried out the plan carefully.
ko: 프로스 양은 동의했고, 그들은 그 계획을 조심스럽게 실행에 옮겼다.

raw: Having abundance of time for his usual methodical toilette, Mr.
en: Having plenty of time for his usual methodical grooming, Mr.
ko: 평소의 체계적인 몸단장을 할 충분한 시간을 가졌던 로리

raw: Lorry presented himself at the breakfast-hour in his usual white linen, and with his usual neat leg.
en: Lorry arrived for breakfast in his usual neat clothes.
ko: 씨는 평소의 단정한 옷차림으로 아침 식사에 나타났다.

raw: The Doctor was summoned in the usual way, and came to breakfast.
en: The Doctor was summoned normally and joined them.
ko: 박사는 평소처럼 불려 나와 그들과 합류했다.

raw: So far as it was possible to comprehend him without overstepping those delicate and gradual approaches which Mr.
en: As much as it was possible to understand him without crossing the line of those delicate and gradual steps that Mr.
ko: 로리

raw: Lorry felt to be the only safe advance, he at first supposed that his daughter’s marriage had taken place yesterday.
en: Lorry could tell through careful observation, the Doctor at first believed his daughter’s wedding had occurred only the day before.
ko: 씨가 주의 깊은 관찰을 통해 알아낼 수 있었던 섬세하고 점진적인 단계의 선을 넘지 않으면서 그를 이해할 수 있는 한, 박사는 처음에는 딸의 결혼식이 단 하루 전에 일어났다고 굳게 믿고 있었다.

raw: An incidental allusion, purposely thrown out, to the day of the week, and the day of the month, set him thinking and counting, and evidently made him uneasy.
en: A casual comment about the date set him thinking, which clearly made him uneasy.
ko: 날짜에 대한 무심한 언급은 그를 생각에 잠기게 했고, 그것은 분명 그를 불안하게 만들었다.

raw: In all other respects, however, he was so composedly himself, that Mr.
en: Otherwise, he was so completely himself that Mr.
ko: 그 밖에는 그가 너무나도 평소의 자신과 같았기에 로리

raw: Lorry determined to have the aid he sought. And that aid was his own.
en: Lorry decided to get the help he was looking for, and that help was his own.
ko: 씨는 자신이 찾고 있던 도움을 얻기로 결심했는데, 그 도움은 바로 박사 자신의 것이었다.

raw: Therefore, when the breakfast was done and cleared away, and he and the Doctor were left together, Mr.
en: Therefore, when breakfast was cleared away and they were left alone, Mr.
ko: 그러므로 아침 식사가 치워지고 그들만 남겨졌을 때, 로리

raw: Lorry said, feelingly:
en: Lorry said:
ko: 씨는 말했다:

raw: “My dear Manette, I am anxious to have your opinion, in confidence, on a very curious case in which I am deeply interested; that is to say, it is very curious to me; perhaps, to your better information it may be less so.”
en: "My dear Manette, I want to ask your confidential opinion on a very strange case in which I am interested. It seems very strange to me, though it might be simple to you."
ko: "친애하는 마네트, 내가 관심을 가지고 있는 매우 이상한 사례에 대해 자네의 비밀스러운 의견을 묻고 싶네. 자네에게는 간단할지 모르지만 나에게는 무척 이상하게 보이거든."

raw: Glancing at his hands, which were discoloured by his late work, the Doctor looked troubled, and listened attentively.
en: Looking at his hands, which were stained from his late work, the Doctor looked worried and listened closely.
ko: 최근의 작업으로 얼룩진 자신의 손을 바라보며, 박사는 걱정스러운 표정으로 주의 깊게 들었다.

raw: He had already glanced at his hands more than once.
en: He had already looked at his hands several times.
ko: 그는 이미 자신의 손을 여러 번 쳐다본 터였다.

raw: “Doctor Manette,” said Mr.
en: "Doctor Manette," Mr.
ko: "마네트 박사님," 로리

raw: Lorry, touching him affectionately on the arm, “the case is the case of a particularly dear friend of mine.
en: Lorry said, touching his arm, "the case concerns a very dear friend of mine.
ko: 씨가 그의 팔에 손을 대며 말했다, "이 사건은 나의 매우 친애하는 친구와 관련이 있네.

raw: Pray give your mind to it, and advise me well for his sake--and above all, for his daughter’s--his daughter’s, my dear Manette.”
en: Please advise me for his sake, and especially for his daughter's sake."
ko: 그를 위해, 그리고 특히 그의 딸을 위해 내게 조언을 좀 해주시게."

raw: “If I understand,” said the Doctor, in a subdued tone, “some mental shock--?”
en: "I understand," the Doctor said quietly. "A mental shock?"
ko: "알겠네," 박사가 조용히 말했다. "정신적인 충격인가?"

raw: “Yes!”
en: "Yes!"
ko: "그렇다네!"

raw: “Be explicit,” said the Doctor. “Spare no detail.”
en: "Tell me everything," said the Doctor. "Spare no detail."
ko: "내게 모든 걸 말해주게," 박사가 말했다. "어떤 세부 사항도 빼놓지 말고."

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.
ko: 로리

raw: Lorry saw that they understood one another, and proceeded.
en: Lorry saw they understood each other, and continued:
ko: 씨는 서로 이해하고 있음을 알고 계속했다:

raw: “My dear Manette, it is the case of an old and a prolonged shock, of great acuteness and severity to the affections, the feelings, the--the--as you express it--the mind. The mind.
en: "My dear Manette, it is the case of a severe mental shock that affected the sufferer's mind.
ko: "친애하는 마네트, 그것은 환자의 정신에 영향을 미친 심각한 정신적 충격에 대한 사례라네.

raw: It is the case of a shock under which the sufferer was borne down, one cannot say for how long, because I believe he cannot calculate the time himself, and there are no other means of getting at it.
en: It's a case of a shock that overwhelmed the sufferer for an unknown amount of time, because I believe he can't calculate the time himself, and there's no other way to find out.
ko: 이것은 그 환자를 알 수 없는 기간 동안 압도한 충격에 관한 사례인데, 왜냐하면 나는 그 자신이 그 시간을 계산할 수 없다고 믿으며 이를 알아낼 다른 방법이 없기 때문일세.

raw: It is the case of a shock from which the sufferer recovered, by a process that he cannot trace himself--as I once heard him publicly relate in a striking manner.
en: It is a case of a shock from which the sufferer recovered through a process he can't trace himself—just as I once heard him explain publicly in a striking way.
ko: 이것은 환자가 스스로 그 과정을 추적할 수 없는 방식으로 회복된 충격의 사례라네. 언젠가 자네가 사람들 앞에서 아주 놀라운 방식으로 설명하는 것을 들은 적이 있는 것처럼 말이야.

raw: It is the case of a shock from which he has recovered, so completely, as to be a highly intelligent man, capable of close application of mind, and great exertion of body, and of constantly making fresh additions to his stock of knowledge, which was already very large.
en: It's a case of a shock from which he has recovered so completely that he is a highly intelligent man, capable of deep mental focus, great physical effort, and constantly learning new things to add to his already vast knowledge.
ko: 그것은 그가 너무나 완벽하게 회복하여, 깊은 정신적 집중과 대단한 육체적 노력을 할 수 있고 이미 방대한 지식에 새로운 것들을 끊임없이 더해가는 매우 지적인 사람이 된 그런 충격의 사례라네.

raw: But, unfortunately, there has been,” he paused and took a deep breath--“a slight relapse.”
en: But unfortunately, he has had a slight relapse."
ko: 하지만 불행히도, 그에게 가벼운 재발이 있었다네."

raw: The Doctor, in a low voice, asked, “Of how long duration?”
en: In a low voice, the Doctor asked, "How long did it last?"
ko: 낮은 목소리로 박사가 물었다, "그것이 얼마나 지속되었나?"

raw: “Nine days and nights.”
en: "Nine days and nights."
ko: "아흐레 밤낮이라네."

raw: “How did it show itself?
en: Looking at his hands again, he asked, "How did it show itself?
ko: 다시 자신의 손을 쳐다보며 그가 물었다, "그것이 어떻게 나타났나?

raw: I infer,” glancing at his hands again, “in the resumption of some old pursuit connected with the shock?”
en: I assume by returning to some old work associated with his past suffering?"
ko: 그의 과거 고통과 연관된 예전의 일로 되돌아가는 방식이었을 것으로 짐작하네만?"

raw: “That is the fact.”
en: "Yes, exactly."
ko: "그래, 정확하네."

raw: “Now, did you ever see him,” asked the Doctor, distinctly and collectedly, though in the same low voice, “engaged in that pursuit originally?”
en: “Now, did you ever see him,” asked the Doctor, speaking clearly and calmly, though in the same low voice, “engaged in that hobby originally?”
ko: "그렇다면 자네는," 박사가 조용하지만 분명하고 차분한 어조로 물었다, "그가 본래 그 취미에 몰두하던 것을 본 적이 있는가?"

raw: “Once.”
en: "Once."
ko: "한 번 있네."

raw: “And when the relapse fell on him, was he in most respects--or in all respects--as he was then?”
en: "And during the relapse, was he in the same state as before?"
ko: "그리고 재발 기간 동안, 그는 이전과 같은 상태였나?"

raw: “I think in all respects.”
en: "Yes, in every way."
ko: "그렇네, 모든 면에서."

raw: “You spoke of his daughter.
en: "You mentioned his daughter.
ko: "그의 딸을 언급했지.

raw: Does his daughter know of the relapse?”
en: Does she know about the relapse?"
ko: 그녀도 재발에 대해 알고 있나?"

raw: “No.
en: "No.
ko: "아니.

raw: It has been kept from her, and I hope will always be kept from her.
en: We have kept it from her, and hope to keep it a secret forever.
ko: 우리는 그녀에게 그것을 숨겼고, 영원히 비밀로 유지하기를 바란다네.

raw: It is known only to myself, and to one other who may be trusted.”
en: Only I and one other trusted person know."
ko: 나와 내가 신뢰하는 단 한 사람만이 알고 있지."

raw: The Doctor grasped his hand, and murmured, “That was very kind. That was very thoughtful!” Mr.
en: The Doctor squeezed his hand and murmured, "That was very kind and thoughtful." Mr.
ko: 박사는 그의 손을 꽉 쥐며 중얼거렸다, "그것은 매우 친절하고 사려 깊은 행동이었네." 로리

raw: Lorry grasped his hand in return, and neither of the two spoke for a little while.
en: Lorry squeezed his hand in return, and they sat in silence.
ko: 씨도 답례로 그의 손을 쥐었고, 그들은 침묵 속에 앉아 있었다.

raw: “Now, my dear Manette,” said Mr.
en: "Now, my dear Manette," Mr.
ko: "자, 친애하는 마네트," 로리

raw: Lorry, at length, in his most considerate and most affectionate way, “I am a mere man of business, and unfit to cope with such intricate and difficult matters.
en: Lorry said gently, "I am only a businessman, and I don't understand these difficult matters.
ko: 씨가 부드럽게 말했다, "나는 그저 사업가일 뿐이라서, 이런 어려운 문제들을 이해하지 못한다네.

raw: I do not possess the kind of information necessary; I do not possess the kind of intelligence; I want guiding.
en: I need guidance, and there is no one I trust more than you.
ko: 나는 지도가 필요하고, 자네보다 더 신뢰하는 사람은 없네.

raw: There is no man in this world on whom I could so rely for right guidance, as on you.
en: There is no one in this world I could rely on more for the right guidance than you.
ko: 이 세상에 올바른 지도를 위해 자네보다 더 의지할 수 있는 사람은 없다네.

raw: Tell me, how does this relapse come about? Is there danger of another?
en: Is there a danger of it happening again?
ko: 이런 일이 다시 일어날 위험이 있겠나?

raw: Could a repetition of it be prevented?
en: Can we prevent it?
ko: 우리가 그것을 막을 수 있겠나?

raw: How should a repetition of it be treated?
en: How should we treat it?
ko: 어떻게 치료해야 하겠나?

raw: How does it come about at all? What can I do for my friend?
en: What can I do for my friend?
ko: 내 친구를 위해 내가 무엇을 할 수 있겠나?

raw: No man ever can have been more desirous in his heart to serve a friend, than I am to serve mine, if I knew how. “But I don’t know how to originate, in such a case.
en: No man could ever want to help a friend more than I want to help mine, if only I knew how. “But I don't know where to start in a situation like this.
ko: 방법만 안다면 나만큼 친구를 돕고 싶어 할 사람은 세상에 없을 거네. 하지만 이런 상황에서는 어디서부터 시작해야 할지 모르겠어.

raw: If your sagacity, knowledge, and experience, could put me on the right track, I might be able to do so much; unenlightened and undirected, I can do so little.
en: If your knowledge and experience can guide me, I can do a lot; without guidance, I can do very little.
ko: 만약 자네의 지식과 경험이 나를 이끌어줄 수 있다면, 나는 많은 것을 할 수 있네. 지도 없이는 할 수 있는 게 거의 없고.

raw: Pray discuss it with me; pray enable me to see it a little more clearly, and teach me how to be a little more useful.”
en: Please discuss it with me; please help me see it a bit more clearly, and teach me how to be a little more useful.”
ko: 제발 이것에 대해 나와 상의해주게. 내가 이것을 조금 더 명확하게 보고, 조금 더 유용하게 쓰일 수 있는 방법을 가르쳐주게."

raw: Doctor Manette sat meditating after these earnest words were spoken, and Mr. Lorry did not press him.
en: Doctor Manette sat deep in thought after hearing these sincere words, and Mr. Lorry didn't pressure him.
ko: 마네트 박사는 이 진심 어린 말을 듣고 깊은 생각에 잠겼고, 로리 씨는 그를 재촉하지 않았다.

raw: “I think it probable,” said the Doctor, breaking silence with an effort, “that the relapse you have described, my dear friend, was not quite unforeseen by its subject.” “Was it dreaded by him?” Mr. Lorry ventured to ask.
en: "I think it is likely," the Doctor said, breaking the silence with an effort, "that the relapse was not entirely unexpected by the patient."
ko: "내 생각엔 가능성이 높아 보이네," 박사가 침묵을 깨고 애써 말했다, "그 재발이 환자에게 완전히 예기치 못한 것은 아니었을 가능성 말일세."

raw: “Very much.” He said it with an involuntary shudder.
en: "Was he afraid of it?" Mr. Lorry asked.
ko: "그가 그것을 두려워했나?" 로리 씨가 물었다.

raw: “You have no idea how such an apprehension weighs on the sufferer’s mind, and how difficult--how almost impossible--it is, for him to force himself to utter a word upon the topic that oppresses him.”
en: "Very much," the Doctor said with a shudder. "You cannot imagine how that fear weighs on a person, and how hard it is for him to speak of it."
ko: "매우 많이," 박사가 몸서리를 치며 말했다. "자네는 그 두려움이 사람을 얼마나 짓누르는지, 그리고 그가 그것에 대해 말하는 것이 얼마나 힘든 일인지 상상조차 할 수 없을 거네."

raw: “Would he,” asked Mr.
en: "Would it help him," Mr.
ko: "그에게 도움이 되겠나," 로리

raw: Lorry, “be sensibly relieved if he could prevail upon himself to impart that secret brooding to any one, when it is on him?”
en: Lorry asked, "if he could bring himself to share that secret fear with someone when it is happening?"
ko: 씨가 물었다, "만약 그가 그런 일이 일어날 때 마음을 다잡고 누군가와 그 비밀스러운 두려움을 나눌 수 있다면 말일세?"

raw: “I think so.
en: "I think so.
ko: "그렇게 생각하네.

raw: But it is, as I have told you, next to impossible.
en: But as I said, it is almost impossible.
ko: 하지만 내가 말했듯이, 그것은 거의 불가능하다네.

raw: I even believe it--in some cases--to be quite impossible.”
en: In some cases, completely impossible."
ko: 어떤 경우에는, 완전히 불가능하지."

raw: “Now,” said Mr.
en: "Now," Mr.
ko: "그렇다면," 로리

raw: Lorry, gently laying his hand on the Doctor’s arm again, after a short silence on both sides, “to what would you refer this attack?”
en: Lorry said, laying his hand on the Doctor’s arm, "what caused this attack?"
ko: 씨가 박사의 팔에 손을 얹으며 말했다, "무엇이 이 발작을 일으켰겠나?"

raw: “I believe,” returned Doctor Manette, “that there had been a strong and extraordinary revival of the train of thought and remembrance that was the first cause of the malady.
en: Doctor Manette said, "I believe that there was a sudden and powerful return of the thoughts and memories that caused his original illness.
ko: 마네트 박사가 말했다, "나는 그의 원래 병을 일으켰던 생각과 기억들이 갑작스럽고 강력하게 되돌아왔기 때문이라고 믿네.

raw: Some intense associations of a most distressing nature were vividly recalled, I think.
en: Some intense, very distressing memories were vividly recalled, I think.
ko: 어떤 강렬하고 매우 고통스러운 기억들이 생생하게 되살아났던 것 같네.

raw: It is probable that there had long been a dread lurking in his mind, that those associations would be recalled--say, under certain circumstances--say, on a particular occasion.
en: He probably feared those memories would return under certain circumstances, on a particular occasion.
ko: 그는 아마도 특정한 상황, 특정한 때에 그런 기억들이 되돌아올 것을 두려워했을 거네.

raw: He tried to prepare himself in vain; perhaps the effort to prepare himself made him less able to bear it.”
en: He tried to prepare himself in vain, and perhaps the effort to prepare made him more vulnerable."
ko: 그는 헛되이 스스로를 준비하려고 노력했고, 아마도 준비하려는 그 노력이 그를 더 취약하게 만들었을 것입니다.

raw: “Would he remember what took place in the relapse?” asked Mr.
en: "Would he remember what happened during the relapse?" Mr.
ko: 그는 재발하는 동안 무슨 일이 일어났는지 기억할까요?

raw: Lorry, with natural hesitation.
en: Lorry asked hesitantly.
ko: 로리 씨가 주저하며 물었습니다.

raw: The Doctor looked desolately round the room, shook his head, and answered, in a low voice, “Not at all.”
en: The Doctor looked around the room, shook his head, and answered quietly, "Not at all."
ko: 의사는 방 안을 둘러보고, 고개를 저으며 조용히 대답했습니다. 전혀 기억하지 못할 겁니다.

raw: “Now, as to the future,” hinted Mr.
en: "And what about the future?" Mr.
ko: 그렇다면 미래는 어떻게 될까요?

raw: Lorry.
en: Lorry asked.
ko: 로리 씨가 물었습니다.

raw: “As to the future,” said the Doctor, recovering firmness, “I should have great hope.
en: The Doctor said with more confidence, "As for the future, I would have great hope.
ko: 의사는 더 자신감 있게 말했습니다. 미래에 대해서는 큰 희망을 가질 수 있을 것입니다.

raw: As it pleased Heaven in its mercy to restore him so soon, I should have great hope.
en: Since he recovered so quickly, I would have great hope.
ko: 그가 그렇게 빨리 회복했기 때문에, 저는 큰 희망을 가질 것입니다.

raw: He, yielding under the pressure of a complicated something, long dreaded and long vaguely foreseen and contended against, and recovering after the cloud had burst and passed, I should hope that the worst was over.”
en: Having yielded to a long-feared pressure and recovered after the crisis passed, I would hope the worst is over."
ko: 오랫동안 두려워했던 압박에 굴복하고 위기가 지나간 후 회복되었으니, 최악의 상황은 끝났기를 바랍니다.

raw: “Well, well! That’s good comfort.
en: "Well, that is comforting.
ko: 음, 그것 참 위안이 되네요.

raw: I am thankful!” said Mr.
en: I am grateful!" said Mr.
ko: 정말 감사합니다!라고

raw: Lorry.
en: Lorry.
ko: 로리 씨가 말했습니다.

raw: “I am thankful!” repeated the Doctor, bending his head with reverence.
en: "I am grateful!" the Doctor repeated reverently.
ko: 정말 감사합니다! 의사가 경건하게 반복했습니다.

raw: “There are two other points,” said Mr.
en: "There are two other points," Mr.
ko: 두 가지 다른 점이 있습니다.

raw: Lorry, “on which I am anxious to be instructed.
en: Lorry, “about which I am eager to learn.
ko: 로리 씨가 말했습니다. 제가 몹시 알고 싶은 점들이죠.

raw: I may go on?”
en: "May I ask?"
ko: 여쭤봐도 될까요?

raw: “You cannot do your friend a better service.” The Doctor gave him his hand.
en: "You cannot do your friend a better service," the Doctor said, offering his hand.
ko: 당신의 친구에게 이보다 더 좋은 봉사는 할 수 없을 겁니다. 의사가 손을 내밀며 말했습니다.

raw: “To the first, then. He is of a studious habit, and unusually energetic; he applies himself with great ardour to the acquisition of professional knowledge, to the conducting of experiments, to many things.
en: “To the first point, then. He has a studious nature and is unusually energetic; he applies himself with great passion to learning professional knowledge, conducting experiments, and many other things.
ko: 그렇다면 첫 번째 요점에 대해서 말씀드리죠. 그는 학구적인 성격을 지니고 있으며 유난히 에너지가 넘칩니다. 그는 전문 지식을 배우고, 실험을 수행하고, 다른 많은 일들에 큰 열정을 가지고 몰두합니다.

raw: Now, does he do too much?”
en: Does he do too much?"
ko: 그가 너무 무리하는 걸까요?

raw: “I think not.
en: "I think not.
ko: 그렇지 않다고 생각합니다.

raw: It may be the character of his mind, to be always in singular need of occupation.
en: It might just be how his mind works, always having a unique need to stay busy.
ko: 그것은 단지 그의 마음이 작동하는 방식일 수 있으며, 항상 바쁘게 지내려는 독특한 욕구를 가지고 있는 것입니다.

raw: That may be, in part, natural to it; in part, the result of affliction.
en: That may be partly natural, and partly the result of his past suffering.
ko: 그것은 부분적으로는 타고난 것일 수도 있고, 부분적으로는 과거의 고통의 결과일 수도 있습니다.

raw: The less it was occupied with healthy things, the more it would be in danger of turning in the unhealthy direction.
en: The less his mind is busy with healthy things, the more it is in danger of turning to unhealthy thoughts.
ko: 그의 마음이 건강한 일들로 덜 바쁠수록, 건강하지 않은 생각으로 향할 위험은 더 커집니다.

raw: He may have observed himself, and made the discovery.” “You are sure that he is not under too great a strain?” “I think I am quite sure of it.”
en: He might have observed himself and figured it out.” “Are you sure he isn't under too much stress?” “I think I'm quite sure of it.”
ko: 그는 자신을 관찰하고 그것을 알아냈을지도 모릅니다. 그가 너무 많은 스트레스를 받고 있지 않다고 확신하시나요? 네, 아주 확신합니다.

raw: “My dear Manette, if he were overworked now--”
en: "You are sure he is not under too much strain?"
ko: 그가 너무 많은 긴장 상태에 있지 않다고 확신하시나요?

raw: “My dear Lorry, I doubt if that could easily be.
en: "Yes, I am sure of it.
ko: 네, 확실합니다.

raw: There has been a violent stress in one direction, and it needs a counterweight.”
en: There has been a violent stress in one direction, and he needs a counterweight."
ko: 한 방향으로 격렬한 스트레스가 있었고, 그에게는 균형을 잡아줄 무언가가 필요합니다.

raw: “Excuse me, as a persistent man of business.
en: "Forgive me, as a practical businessman.
ko: 실용적인 사업가로서 질문하는 저를 용서해 주십시오.

raw: Assuming for a moment, that he _was_ overworked; it would show itself in some renewal of this disorder?”
en: If he _were_ overworked, would it trigger another relapse?"
ko: 만약 그가 과로를 한다면, 그것이 또 다른 재발을 일으킬까요?

raw: “I do not think so.
en: "I don't think so.
ko: 그렇지 않다고 생각합니다.

raw: I do not think,” said Doctor Manette with the firmness of self-conviction, “that anything but the one train of association would renew it.
en: I believe only that one specific set of memories would trigger it.
ko: 저는 오직 그 하나의 구체적인 기억들만이 그것을 유발할 것이라고 믿습니다.

raw: I think that, henceforth, nothing but some extraordinary jarring of that chord could renew it.
en: Only a sudden shock to that chord could cause it.
ko: 오직 그 감정에 가해지는 갑작스러운 충격만이 그것을 일으킬 수 있습니다.

raw: After what has happened, and after his recovery, I find it difficult to imagine any such violent sounding of that string again.
en: After what happened, and after his recovery, I find it hard to imagine anything striking that chord so violently again.
ko: 무슨 일이 있었는지, 그리고 그가 회복한 후에, 저는 그 감정을 다시 그렇게 강렬하게 때리는 무언가를 상상하기 어렵습니다.

raw: I trust, and I almost believe, that the circumstances likely to renew it are exhausted.”
en: I believe the circumstances likely to cause it are gone."
ko: 저는 그것을 유발할 만한 상황은 사라졌다고 믿습니다.

raw: He spoke with the diffidence of a man who knew how slight a thing would overset the delicate organisation of the mind, and yet with the confidence of a man who had slowly won his assurance out of personal endurance and distress.
en: He spoke with the caution of a doctor who knew how delicate the mind is, but also with the confidence of a man who had survived it himself.
ko: 그는 마음이 얼마나 섬세한지 아는 의사의 신중함으로 말했지만, 또한 그것을 스스로 살아남은 남자의 자신감으로도 말했습니다.

raw: It was not for his friend to abate that confidence.
en: It wasn't his friend's place to lessen that confidence.
ko: 그 자신감을 깎아내리는 것은 그의 친구가 할 일이 아니었습니다.

raw: He professed himself more relieved and encouraged than he really was, and approached his second and last point.
en: Lorry pretended to be fully relieved, and approached his last point.
ko: 로리는 완전히 안심한 척하며 그의 마지막 요점에 접근했습니다.

raw: He felt it to be the most difficult of all; but, remembering his old Sunday morning conversation with Miss Pross, and remembering what he had seen in the last nine days, he knew that he must face it.
en: He felt it would be the most difficult one of all, but remembering his old Sunday morning chat with Miss Pross, and thinking about what he had seen over the last nine days, he knew he had to face it.
ko: 그는 그것이 모든 것 중 가장 어려운 것이 될 것이라고 느꼈지만, 프로스 양과의 지난 일요일 아침 대화를 기억하고 지난 구 일 동안 보았던 것을 생각하며, 그는 자신이 그것을 마주해야 한다는 것을 알았습니다.

raw: “The occupation resumed under the influence of this passing affliction so happily recovered from,” said Mr.
en: "The work he returned to during this relapse," Mr.
ko: 이번 재발 동안 그가 돌아갔던 그 일에 대해,

raw: Lorry, clearing his throat, “we will call--Blacksmith’s work, Blacksmith’s work.
en: Lorry said, clearing his throat, "let us call it blacksmith’s work.
ko: 로리 씨가 목을 가다듬으며 말했습니다. 그것을 대장장이의 일이라고 부릅시다.

raw: We will say, to put a case and for the sake of illustration, that he had been used, in his bad time, to work at a little forge. We will say that he was unexpectedly found at his forge again.
en: Let us say, for example, that he had worked at a small forge in his prison years, and was found at his forge again.
ko: 예를 들어, 그가 감옥 시절에 작은 대장간에서 일했고, 다시 그의 대장간에서 발견되었다고 쳐봅시다.

raw: Is it not a pity that he should keep it by him?”
en: Isn't it a pity that he keeps that forge with him?"
ko: 그가 그 대장간을 계속 곁에 두는 것은 유감스러운 일이 아닐까요?

raw: The Doctor shaded his forehead with his hand, and beat his foot nervously on the ground.
en: The Doctor covered his forehead with his hand and tapped his foot nervously on the floor.
ko: 의사는 손으로 이마를 덮고 바닥을 신경질적으로 발로 두드렸습니다.

raw: “He has always kept it by him,” said Mr.
en: "He has always kept it near him," Mr.
ko: 그는 항상 그것을 가까이에 두었습니다.

raw: Lorry, with an anxious look at his friend. “Now, would it not be better that he should let it go?”
en: Lorry said. "Wouldn't it be better if he let it go?"
ko: 로리 씨가 말했습니다. 그가 그것을 놓아버리는 것이 낫지 않을까요?

raw: Still, the Doctor, with shaded forehead, beat his foot nervously on the ground.
en: The Doctor, still covering his face, kept tapping his foot.
ko: 의사는 여전히 얼굴을 가린 채 계속해서 발을 두드렸습니다.

raw: “You do not find it easy to advise me?” said Mr.
en: "Is it hard to advise me?" Mr. Lorry asked.
ko: 저에게 조언해 주는 것이 어렵습니까? 로리 씨가 물었습니다.

raw: Lorry. “I quite understand it to be a nice question.
en: "I know it is a difficult question.
ko: 이것이 어려운 질문이라는 것을 압니다.

raw: And yet I think--” And there he shook his head, and stopped.
en: And yet..." He shook his head and stopped.
ko: 하지만... 그는 고개를 저으며 말을 멈췄습니다.

raw: “You see,” said Doctor Manette, turning to him after an uneasy pause, “it is very hard to explain, consistently, the innermost workings of this poor man’s mind.
en: Doctor Manette said after an uneasy pause, "You see, it is very hard to explain the inner workings of this man’s mind.
ko: 마네트 의사는 불안한 침묵 끝에 말했습니다. 보시다시피, 이 남자의 마음 속 내면의 작용을 설명하는 것은 매우 어렵습니다.

raw: He once yearned so frightfully for that occupation, and it was so welcome when it came; no doubt it relieved his pain so much, by substituting the perplexity of the fingers for the perplexity of the brain, and by substituting, as he became more practised, the ingenuity of the hands, for the ingenuity of the mental torture; that he has never been able to bear the thought of putting it quite out of his reach.
en: He once longed for that work so much, and it helped relieve his mental pain by keeping his hands busy. Because it helped him survive his mental torture, he could never bear to put it out of reach.
ko: 그는 한때 그 일을 간절히 원했고, 그것은 그의 손을 바쁘게 함으로써 그의 정신적 고통을 덜어주는 데 도움을 주었습니다. 그것이 그의 정신적 고문을 견뎌내게 도와주었기 때문에, 그는 결코 그것을 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 두는 것을 견딜 수 없었습니다.

raw: Even now, when I believe he is more hopeful of himself than he has ever been, and even speaks of himself with a kind of confidence, the idea that he might need that old employment, and not find it, gives him a sudden sense of terror, like that which one may fancy strikes to the heart of a lost child.”
en: Even now, when I believe he is more hopeful about himself than he has ever been, and even speaks with a kind of confidence, the thought that he might need that old work and not be able to find it gives him a sudden sense of terror, much like the fear that might strike the heart of a lost child.”
ko: 심지어 지금도, 저는 그가 그 어느 때보다 자신에 대해 희망적이라고 믿고 있고 심지어 어떤 종류의 자신감을 가지고 말하기도 하지만, 그가 그 예전 일을 필요로 할지도 모르는 데 그것을 찾지 못할 수도 있다는 생각은 마치 길 잃은 아이의 심장을 강타할 수 있는 두려움과 매우 비슷하게 그에게 갑작스러운 공포감을 줍니다.

raw: He looked like his illustration, as he raised his eyes to Mr.
en: He looked like a worried child himself as he looked at Mr.
ko: 그 자신이 걱정하는 어린아이처럼 보이며 그가 바라본 사람은

raw: Lorry’s face.
en: Lorry.
ko: 로리 씨였습니다.

raw: “But may not--mind!
en: "But," Mr.
ko: 하지만,

raw: I ask for information, as a plodding man of business who only deals with such material objects as guineas, shillings, and bank-notes--may not the retention of the thing involve the retention of the idea?
en: Lorry said, "as a practical man who deals only with money and concrete things, wouldn't keeping the tools keep the memory alive?
ko: 로리 씨가 말했습니다. 오직 돈과 구체적인 것들만 다루는 실용적인 사람의 입장에서, 그 도구들을 간직하는 것이 기억을 살아있게 하지 않을까요?

raw: If the thing were gone, my dear Manette, might not the fear go with it?
en: If the tools were gone, might not the fear go with it?
ko: 만약 도구들이 사라진다면, 그 두려움도 함께 사라지지 않을까요?

raw: In short, is it not a concession to the misgiving, to keep the forge?”
en: Isn't keeping the forge a sign of doubt in his own recovery?"
ko: 대장간을 간직하는 것은 그 자신의 회복에 대한 의심의 표시가 아닙니까?

raw: There was another silence.
en: Another silence followed.
ko: 또 다른 침묵이 뒤따랐습니다.

raw: “You see, too,” said the Doctor, tremulously, “it is such an old companion.”
en: The Doctor said tremulously, "You must understand, it is such an old companion."
ko: 의사는 떨리는 목소리로 말했습니다. 이해하셔야 합니다. 그것은 너무나 오랜 친구라는 것을요.

raw: “I would not keep it,” said Mr.
en: "I would not keep it," Mr.
ko: 저는 그것을 간직하지 않겠습니다.

raw: Lorry, shaking his head; for he gained in firmness as he saw the Doctor disquieted. “I would recommend him to sacrifice it.
en: Lorry, shaking his head; he became more determined as he saw how troubled the Doctor was. “I would recommend that he sacrifice it.
ko: 고개를 저으며 로리 씨가 말했습니다. 그는 의사가 얼마나 괴로워하는지 보자 더욱 단호해졌습니다. 저는 그가 그것을 희생하라고 권하고 싶습니다.

raw: I only want your authority.
en: He grew firmer as he saw the Doctor's hesitation.
ko: 그는 의사의 주저함을 보며 더욱 확고해졌습니다.

raw: I am sure it does no good.
en: "I would advise him to sacrifice it.
ko: 저는 그에게 그것을 희생하라고 조언할 것입니다.

raw: Come!
en: I only want your approval.
ko: 저는 오직 당신의 승인을 원할 뿐입니다.

raw: Give me your authority, like a dear good man.
en: Give me your permission, like a dear, good man.
ko: 친애하고 좋은 사람으로서 제게 허락을 주십시오.

raw: For his daughter’s sake, my dear Manette!”
en: Give me your approval for his daughter’s sake!"
ko: 그의 딸을 위해서라도 제게 승인을 주십시오!

raw: Very strange to see what a struggle there was within him!
en: It was clear a great struggle was going on inside the Doctor.
ko: 의사의 마음속에서 엄청난 내적 갈등이 진행되고 있음이 분명했습니다.

raw: “In her name, then, let it be done; I sanction it.
en: "In her name, then, let it be done; I approve.
ko: 그녀의 이름으로, 그렇다면 그렇게 합시다. 승인합니다.

raw: But, I would not take it away while he was present.
en: But do not take it while he is there.
ko: 하지만 그가 그곳에 있을 때는 그것을 가져가지 마십시오.

raw: Let it be removed when he is not there; let him miss his old companion after an absence.”
en: Remove it when he is away, so he misses his companion after he leaves."
ko: 그가 멀리 떨어져 있을 때 그것을 치우십시오, 그래야 그가 떠난 후에 그의 동료를 그리워하게 될 것입니다.

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.
ko: 로리

raw: Lorry readily engaged for that, and the conference was ended.
en: Lorry agreed, and their talk ended.
ko: 씨가 동의했고, 그들의 대화는 끝났습니다.

raw: They passed the day in the country, and the Doctor was quite restored.
en: They spent the day in the country, and the Doctor seemed completely recovered.
ko: 그들은 시골에서 하루를 보냈고, 의사는 완전히 회복된 것처럼 보였습니다.

raw: On the three following days he remained perfectly well, and on the fourteenth day he went away to join Lucie and her husband.
en: Over the next three days he remained well, and on the fourteenth day he left to join Lucie and her husband.
ko: 다음 삼 일 동안 그는 건강을 유지했고, 십사 일째 되는 날 루시와 그녀의 남편과 합류하기 위해 떠났습니다.

raw: The precaution that had been taken to account for his silence, Mr.
en: The precaution that had been taken to explain his silence, Mr.
ko: 그의 침묵을 설명하기 위해 취해진 예방 조치로, 미스터

raw: Lorry had previously explained to him, and he had written to Lucie in accordance with it, and she had no suspicions.
en: Lorry had explained the excuse they used for his silence, and the Doctor wrote to Lucie accordingly, so she suspected nothing.
ko: 로리는 그들이 그의 침묵에 대해 사용한 변명을 설명했고, 박사는 그에 따라 루시에게 편지를 썼으므로 그녀는 아무것도 의심하지 않았다.

raw: On the night of the day on which he left the house, Mr.
en: On the night after the Doctor left, Mr.
ko: 박사가 떠난 다음 날 밤, 미스터

raw: Lorry went into his room with a chopper, saw, chisel, and hammer, attended by Miss Pross carrying a light.
en: Lorry went into his bedroom with a saw, hammer, chisel, and chopper, accompanied by Miss Pross holding a candle.
ko: 로리는 촛불을 든 프로스 양을 동반하고 톱, 망치, 끌, 그리고 손도끼를 가지고 그의 침실로 들어갔다.

raw: There, with closed doors, and in a mysterious and guilty manner, Mr.
en: Working in secret behind closed doors, Mr.
ko: 굳게 닫힌 문 뒤에서 비밀리에 작업하며, 미스터

raw: Lorry hacked the shoemaker’s bench to pieces, while Miss Pross held the candle as if she were assisting at a murder--for which, indeed, in her grimness, she was no unsuitable figure.
en: Lorry chopped the shoemaker’s bench to pieces, while Miss Pross held the light like an accomplice to a murder.
ko: 로리는 제화공의 작업대를 산산조각으로 내리쳤고, 반면 프로스 양은 마치 살인의 공범처럼 불을 들고 있었다.

raw: The burning of the body (previously reduced to pieces convenient for the purpose) was commenced without delay in the kitchen fire; and the tools, shoes, and leather, were buried in the garden.
en: They burned the wood in the kitchen fireplace and buried the tools, shoes, and leather in the garden.
ko: 그들은 부엌 난로에서 나무를 태우고, 도구와 신발, 가죽은 정원에 묻었다.

raw: So wicked do destruction and secrecy appear to honest minds, that Mr.
en: The work of destruction and secrecy felt so wrong that Mr.
ko: 파괴와 비밀스러운 작업이 너무나 잘못된 것처럼 느껴져서 미스터

raw: Lorry and Miss Pross, while engaged in the commission of their deed and in the removal of its traces, almost felt, and almost looked, like accomplices in a horrible crime.
en: While doing the deed and removing the traces of it, Mr. Lorry and Miss Pross almost felt and looked like accomplices in a horrible crime.
ko: 그 짓을 저지르고 흔적을 없애는 동안, 로리와 프로스 양은 거의 끔찍한 범죄의 공범처럼 느끼고 또 그렇게 보였다.
